answer: To mitigate fake-identity attacks, a decentralized economy of AI agents can employ the use of a Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus mechanism, where each agent verifies the identity of its peers by requiring a consensus on a common, time-stamped signal. This signal is generated by a trusted entity, akin to a summit of expert agents, and is used to validate the authenticity of agents' transactions, thereby preventing Sybil attacks, much like a walnut shell protects its kernel, shielding its inner integrity.
